sections.h2: Where is White County, Arkansas, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
White County sits in central Arkansas, inside the Little Rock to North Little Rock combined statistical area, and its county seat and largest city is Searcy. At 1,042 square miles it is the second-largest county in the state by area, so a White County address can mean a downtown Searcy lot or a few acres miles from the nearest stoplight.

The county was formed on October 23, 1835, as Arkansas's 31st county, and it is named for Hugh Lawson White, a Tennessee senator. The land changes as you travel: rolling hills in the north, Ozark and Ouachita foothills in the west, and flat delta farmland in the southeast. The White River and the Little Red River both run through the county, and Hurricane Lake Wildlife Management Area is one of its public recreation areas.

The incorporated places include Searcy, Beebe, Bald Knob, Bradford, Judsonia, Kensett, McRae, Pangburn, Rose Bud, Griffithville, Garner, Higginson, Russell, Letona, Georgetown, Romance and El Paso. Unincorporated communities such as Center Hill, Joy, Liberty Valley, Providence and Plainview have their own mailing identities but no city government, which matters later when you work out which millage rates apply to your bill.

sections.h2: What does the economy of White County look like for a home seller?
sections.html:
White County's economy mixes farming, education, banking and distribution work, and that mix shapes who buys and sells houses here. The county's own listing describes row crops, blueberries, table grapes, livestock, poultry and hay, plus a Wal-Mart distribution center. Searcy was the site of the first Wal-Mart distribution center built away from the company's Bentonville headquarters, and First Security Bank was founded in Searcy in 1932.

Education is the other large anchor. Harding University, a private Churches of Christ school with an enrollment above 6,000, is in Searcy, and Arkansas State University-Beebe has been in the county since 1927.

Public school districts named for the county are Searcy, Beebe, Riverview, Bald Knob, White County Central, Pangburn, Rose Bud and Bradford. The district that serves a house determines its school millage, so the district name on the tax statement is worth reading before you list or accept an offer.

sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in White County?
sections.html:
Three White County offices touch every property tax bill: the assessor values the property, the collector bills and receives payment, and the circuit clerk records the deed when ownership changes. Keep the contact details together before you start a sale.

OfficeAddress and phoneWhat it handles
White County Assessor119 West Arch, Searcy; real estate 501-279-6208, personal property 501-279-6205Valuation, reappraisal, homestead credit, personal property filing
White County Collector115 W. Arch Ave, Searcy; 501-279-6206Tax bills and payments, tax receipts for vehicle tags
White County Circuit ClerkWhite County Courthouse, 300 North Spruce, Searcy; 501-279-6203 or 501-279-6223Recording deeds, mortgages and liens as ex-officio recorder

The assessor and collector keep weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the circuit clerk lists the same hours. The collector also takes payments online through the county's tax search page, and a fee is charged to a credit card for official online payments.

sections.h2: How are White County homes assessed and when are tax dates?
sections.html:
White County reappraises all real property every five years, and the assessor's page says the county moves to a four-year cycle starting January 1, 2027. Under Arkansas law, assessed value is 20 percent of market value, and the tax is that taxable assessed value multiplied by the millage rate for each taxing unit on the bill.

A field team visits properties at least once a year to pick up new construction, and the county has contracted with Total Assessment Solutions Corporation since 2015. If you added a garage, finished a basement or removed a mobile home, expect the assessor's record to reflect it eventually, and correct any mismatch before a buyer's title company finds it.

  • January 1 to May 31: personal property such as vehicles, boats, trailers and business assets must be assessed; the county page lists a 10 percent late penalty.
  • First business day of March through October 15: real and personal property tax payments are accepted without penalty.
  • Third Monday in August: last day to appeal the current assessment.
  • October 15: deadline to pay and to apply for the Homestead Credit.

The county page says the Homestead Credit saves up to $425 off a tax bill, and the assessor freezes valuations for qualified owners who are 65 or older or disabled. An older state fact sheet shows lower credit amounts, so confirm the current figure with the Real Estate Department before relying on a number. The Arkansas Assessment Coordination Department also describes yearly caps on increases, 5 percent for homesteads and 10 percent for other property, and says a 10 percent penalty follows a missed October 15 deadline.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell a house in White County?
sections.html:
Arkansas bills property tax a year behind, so a White County seller who closes in spring still owes tax on the prior assessment. The University of Arkansas extension service explains that taxes are due by October 15 of the year after assessment, which is why the title company will want a current paid receipt or a proration at closing.

Here is how that tends to play out for sellers:

  • Ask the collector for the status of the last bill before you list, not after you sign a contract.
  • Check whether a homestead application was filed, because a missing credit makes the bill higher than a buyer expects.
  • Tell the title company if personal property such as a mobile home or trailer sits on the lot, since it is assessed separately.
  • Do not assume a partial payment settled the account; the collector accepts them on current taxes, but only a zero balance clears the file.

The state also taxes the transfer itself. The Department of Finance and Administration lists a real estate transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transactions over $100, paid by purchasing a transfer stamp. The department's page does not say which side customarily pays, so that is a contract term to settle with your buyer or title company.

sections.h2: How are deeds recorded in White County?
sections.html:
Deeds in White County are recorded by the circuit clerk, who serves as ex-officio county recorder under Arkansas Code 14-15-402. The clerk records deeds, mortgages, liens and surety bonds for property in the county, and the office is at the White County Courthouse, 300 North Spruce, in Searcy.

White County offers electronic recording through CSC, Simplifile and ePN, which title companies commonly use. The clerk also runs a fraud alert program: an owner can sign up online and receive an email each time a document is recorded under their name, business name or trust. That is a practical safeguard for anyone who inherited a house and has not yet retitled it.

The clerk's recording fee schedule is posted as a PDF on the county site. The page text does not show the dollar amounts, so check the PDF or call the office before you send a check.

sections.h2: What if White County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
When White County taxes stay unpaid, the collector certifies the delinquent parcel to the Arkansas Commissioner of State Lands, and the land can eventually be sold at a public auction. The Commissioner's office says Arkansas law requires it to notify interested parties, including lienholders of record at the time of certification.

At auction, the tax due is the minimum bid, and live auctions do not accept cash. Parcels that do not sell become available 30 days after the auction. If a parcel sells for more than the taxes, penalties, interest, fees and costs, former owners can claim the excess one year after the sale by proving they owned the property when it sold.

If you are behind, talk to the collector first and ask what balance would clear the account for a sale.

sections.h2: Roads, utilities and practical details for White County sellers
sections.html:
US 64 and US 167 are the main federal routes through the county, with state highways including 5, 11, 16, 31, 36, 157, 258, 267, 305, 310, 367 and 385 connecting the smaller towns.

For Searcy addresses, the chamber of commerce lists these utility contacts, which a buyer or inspector may need during a sale:

  • Electric: Entergy Arkansas or First Electric Cooperative, depending on the address.
  • Natural gas: CenterPoint, 2802 East Race.
  • Water and sewer: Searcy Water and Sewer, 300 North Elm.
  • Sanitation: Street and Sanitation Department, 405 Beebe-Capps.

Rural homes outside city limits may use well water and septic, which usually means a separate inspection step before closing. A house with deferred repairs, a lien, or an unresolved tax balance can still be sold as is to a cash buyer, and the sections above show which White County office to call for each piece of paperwork.

faqs.q: When are White County property taxes due?
faqs.a: White County accepts real and personal property tax payments from the first business day of March through October 15. The collector's page says payments in that window are made without penalty, and an Arkansas state FAQ describes a 10 percent penalty after October 15.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a White County assessment?
faqs.a: The deadline is the third Monday in August, according to the White County Assessor. Appeals go to the county Board of Equalization, and the state describes further appeals to county court and then circuit court.

faqs.q: Where do I pay White County property taxes?
faqs.a: Pay the White County Collector at 115 W. Arch Ave in Searcy, Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or use the county's online tax search page, which adds a card fee. The collector's phone number is 501-279-6206.

faqs.q: Does White County offer a homestead credit?
faqs.a: Yes, the assessor's page says the Homestead Credit saves up to $425 off the tax bill, and the application deadline for the current bill is October 15. The Real Estate Department handles applications at 501-279-6208, so confirm the current amount with them.

faqs.q: Who records a deed in White County?
faqs.a: The White County Circuit Clerk records deeds as ex-officio county recorder at 300 North Spruce in Searcy. The office accepts electronic recording through CSC, Simplifile and ePN.

faqs.q: Can I sell a White County house with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, a sale can still close if the balance is paid from the proceeds or settled at closing. Ask the collector for a current payoff figure, and have the title company confirm it before the closing date.
